producer: Revision/theory/wolfram/verify_scope.wls (WolframScript, exact; no shared code with the sympy checker or with RevisionFieldTheory.wl)
spec: Revision/SPEC.md sections 1-6: scope of the non-triviality, quantisation and energy statements
metric: the corrected metric of 2026-10-16: diag(E^(-2 a4) b4 Cot[z]^2, E^(2 a4) (x3), -1, -E^(-2 a4) b4 (Sin[z]^2)^(1/6) (x3)), z = 6 H x0 real
coordinates: the author's coordinates x0..x7: x0 = the hidden, space-like direction, z = 6 H x0 real (-Infinity < z < Infinity); x1, x2, x3 = 3-space; x4 = time; x5, x6, x7 = the exponentially deflating extra times

checks.name: zero_test_controls
checks.detail: the exact zero test of this file returns True on identities and False on nonzero expressions: (Sin z^2)^(1/2) - Sin z is not zero (no sign of Sin z is assumed), w^12 - Sin^2, sgn^2 - 1, Cosh^2 - Sinh^2 - 1 are zero, sgn - 1 and Cosh - 1 are not

checks.name: fixture_gammas
checks.detail: gammas.json: {gamma^a, gamma^b} = 2 eta^ab I16 (eta = diag(1,1,1,1,-1,-1,-1,-1), order x0..x7), C = gamma^(x0) gamma^(x1) gamma^(x2) gamma^(x3), B = -i C gamma^(x4)

checks.name: boosted_frame_reproduces_metric
checks.detail: frame boosted in the (x4, x0) plane with rapidity b = beta x4 + b0: e'^(x4) = Cosh[b] e^(x4) + Sinh[b] e^(x0), e'^(x0) = Sinh[b] e^(x4) + Cosh[b] e^(x0), the other e'^(a) = e^(a) of the diagonal vielbein (f0 = E^-a4 b4^(1/2) Cot z, f_i = E^a4, f_t = E^-a4 b4^(1/2) (Sin z^2)^(1/12)); e'^T eta e' equals the corrected metric for all 64 entries and every real z

checks.name: boosted_frame_canonical_connection
checks.detail: canonical spin connection of the boosted frame (Christoffel symbols computed here from the corrected metric): the vielbein postulate d_mu e'^a_nu - Gamma^lam_mu,nu e'^a_lam + omega_mu^a_b e'^b_nu = 0 holds for all 512 components (0 failures), omega_mu ab antisymmetric

checks.name: boosted_frame_gammaOmega_formula
checks.detail: gamma'^mu Omega'_mu = (cg - beta/2) (Cosh[b] gamma^(x0) - Sinh[b] gamma^(x4)) + vg (Cosh[b] gamma^(x4) - Sinh[b] gamma^(x0)) exactly for symbolic a4[x4], b4[x4], H, beta, b0, every real z, cg = (3/2) H E^a4 b4^(-1/2), vg = b4'/b4 - a4'/2; control: the same code for the unboosted (diagonal) frame gives cg gamma^(x0) + vg gamma^(x4)

checks.name: boosted_frame_removes_only_the_H_term
checks.detail: for a frame boosted in the (x4, x0) plane with ANY rapidity function b(x4): gamma'^mu Omega'_mu = c0 gamma^(x0) + c4 gamma^(x4) with Cosh[b] c4 + Sinh[b] c0 = vg = b4'/b4 - a4'/2 exactly, so gamma'^mu Omega'_mu = 0 forces b4'/b4 = a4'/2 (b4 proportional to E^(a4/2)): for general a4, b4 no boost in this plane removes the spin-connection term. The rapidity with b' = 2 cg = 3 H E^a4 b4^(-1/2) removes the cg part: gamma'^mu Omega'_mu = vg (Cosh[b] gamma^(x4) - Sinh[b] gamma^(x0)) for every H > 0, a4[x4], b4[x4] (exact; b given by its derivative); the value cg gamma^(x0) + vg gamma^(x4) is a property of the diagonal vielbein, its cg part is not a frame-independent part of the field equation. Omega'_mu is nonzero for mu = x0, x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, x6, x7

checks.name: boosted_frame_curvature_nonzero
checks.detail: in the boosted frame (b' = 2 cg) the spinor curvature F'_x5x0 = d_x5 Omega'_x0 - d_x0 Omega'_x5 + [Omega'_x5, Omega'_x0] is nonzero for general a4, b4: Omega' does not vanish; no frame can make Omega vanish where the metric is curved, because the curvature of the spin connection is (1/2) R_ab,mu,nu S^ab (the corrected metric is flat only for special a4, b4, such as a4 = 0, b4 = H^2 x4^2)

checks.name: rescaling_removes_the_connection_term
checks.detail: diagonal frame: gamma^mu Omega_mu = cg gamma^(x0) + vg gamma^(x4); for Psi = E^(a4/2) b4^(-1) (Sin z^2)^(-1/8) chi with 16 arbitrary functions chi_A(x0, ..., x7), gamma^mu D_mu Psi - E^(a4/2) b4^(-1) (Sin z^2)^(-1/8) gamma^mu d_mu chi = 0 component by component (computed on the functions themselves, every real z): in the variables chi the field equation has no spin-connection term

checks.name: rescaled_equation_quadratic_potential
checks.detail: U = (lambda/2) S^2: S[E^(a4/2) b4^(-1) (Sin z^2)^(-1/8) chi] = E^a4 b4^(-2) |Sin z|^(-1/2) S[chi] (the factor is real and positive), so the rescaled equation is gamma^mu d_mu chi = (m + lambda E^a4 S[chi]/(b4^2 |Sin z|^(1/2))) chi: the spin-connection term is removed completely for U = 0 and becomes an x0- and x4-dependent coupling for U != 0

checks.name: gammaOmega_sees_the_hidden_block
checks.detail: diagonal frame: gamma^mu Omega_mu = (3/2) H E^a4 b4^(-1/2) gamma^(x0) + (b4'/b4 - a4'/2) gamma^(x4) contains a4 (unlike the metric of 2026-10-14, where it was 3 H gamma^(x0) + (3/4)(b4'/b4) gamma^(x4)): its gamma^(x0) coefficient is (3/2) H times the inverse scale factor E^a4 b4^(-1/2) of the hidden block, which grows as the block deflates; Riemann computed here from the metric: R^x4_x4 = 7 a4'^2 - a4'' - 4 a4' b4'/b4 + 2 b4''/b4 - (b4'/b4)^2, R^x1_x1 = -a4'^2 + a4'' + 2 a4' b4'/b4, R^x0_x0 = R^x5_x5 = -3 Cb + a4'^2 - a4'' - (5/2) a4' b4'/b4 + (1/2) b4''/b4 + (1/2)(b4'/b4)^2, Cb = H^2 E^(2 a4)/b4

checks.name: connection_free_lagrangian_same_equations
checks.detail: diagonal frame: {gamma^mu, Omega_mu} = 0 for each mu, so the canonical spin connection drops out of the symmetrised Lagrangian (L(Omega) = L(Omega = 0)) and the Euler-Lagrange equations are those of the connection-free symmetric Lagrangian; (1/(2 sqrt|g|)) d_mu(sqrt|g| gamma^mu) = gamma^mu Omega_mu = cg gamma^(x0) + vg gamma^(x4) (sqrt|g| = sgn E^-a4 b4^2 Cot z (Sin z^2)^(1/4)): the half-density term

checks.name: spin_connection_in_the_energy_momentum_tensor
checks.detail: homogeneous configuration Phi(x4), diagonal frame: the connection part of K^x4_x1 = (1/2)(Phibar gamma^x4 D_x1 Phi - D_x1 Phibar gamma^x4 Phi) is (1/2) Phibar {gamma^x4, Omega_x1} Phi = 0 (3-space does not depend on x0 in the corrected metric), but that of K^x4_x5 is (1/2) Phibar {gamma^x4, Omega_x5} Phi = (1/2) H (Sin z^2)^(1/12) Phibar gamma^(x4) gamma^(x0) gamma^(x5) Phi, not identically zero: the canonical spin connection reaches the energy-momentum tensor through the extra times

checks.name: good_sector_hermiticity_up_to_the_brane_flux
checks.detail: curved good-sector mode operator at k = 0, h = -i m gamma^(x4) + i gamma^(x4) gamma^(x0) E^a4 b4^(-1/2) (Tan[z] d_x0 + (3/2) H) - i vg: for arbitrary complex u(x0), v(x0) (32 real functions) and every real z, sqrt|g| (u^dagger h v - (h u)^dagger v) = d_x0 (sgn b4^(3/2) (Sin z^2)^(1/4) u^dagger M0 v) - i (d_x4 sqrt|g|) u^dagger v, M0 = i gamma^(x4) gamma^(x0), exactly; d_x4 sqrt|g| = 2 vg sqrt|g| (the anti-Hermitian term -i vg compensates the x4 dependence of the measure, so d/dx4 Integrate[sqrt|g| u^dagger v] = the x0 boundary term for solutions); the boundary term vanishes where Sin z = 0 but not where Cos z = 0 (|Sin z| = 1, the degenerate points z = Pi/2 + n Pi of g00): for gamma^(x4) gamma^(x0) u = u, u^dagger M0 u = 2*I (|u|^2 = 2). The conservation (symmetry of h for Integrate[sqrt|g| u^dagger v]) holds only with boundary conditions at the degenerate points

checks.name: good_sector_x0_independent_modes_without_boundary_condition
checks.detail: on x0-independent good-sector functions (finite norm on each interval between degenerate points: Integrate[Cot[6 H x0] Sin[6 H x0]^(1/2), {x0, 0, Pi/(12 H)}] = 1/(3*H)) the curved mode operator of Psi is A - i vg with the matrix A(x4) = -i m gamma^(x4) + i cg gamma^(x4) gamma^(x0), so Psi = E^(a4/2) b4^(-1) chi where chi evolves with A alone (i d4 chi = A chi): A is not Hermitian, A^2 = (m^2 - cg^2) I16 with cg = (3/2) H E^a4 b4^(-1/2): wherever m^2 < cg^2 the instantaneous frequencies are imaginary; on the record's history a4 = H x4, b4 = E^(4 H x4/3) cg = (3/2) H E^(H x4/3) grows, so every mass falls below it at late x4: without a boundary condition at the degenerate points the good sector contains growing modes

checks.name: extra_time_growth_rates_unbounded
checks.detail: flat 4+4 space (or frozen coefficients): h_k = -i m gamma^(x4) - gamma^(x4) Sum[k_a gamma^(a)] has h_k^2 = (k0^2 + k1^2 + k2^2 + k3^2 - k5^2 - k6^2 - k7^2 + m^2) I16; with k5 = K5 the growth rate Sqrt[-k0^2 - k1^2 - k2^2 - k3^2 + K5^2 - m^2] is unbounded as K5 -> Infinity: the Cauchy problem for data depending on x5, x6, x7 is not well posed in Hadamard's sense, although the slices x4 = const are non-characteristic

checks.name: commuting_field_energy_unbounded_below
checks.detail: dirac16complex00, flat frame, good sector, U = 0, m = 2, (k0, k1, k2, k3) = (4, 1, 2, 0), E = 5: [B, h_k] = 0; the E = 5 eigenspace has dimension 8 and the form u^dagger B u on it has inertia {4, 4}; the positive-frequency solutions Phi = c u E^(i (k.x - 5 x4)) (field equation verified) with B u = -u and B u = +u, |u| = 1, have energy density rho = -T^x4_x4 = -5*cc^2 and 5*cc^2 and charge density Phi^dagger B Phi = -cc^2 and cc^2 (cc = |c|): the classical energy is unbounded below already for U = 0, and the U(1) charge is indefinite (only its local law d_mu (sqrt|g| J^mu) = 0 is proved; the total charge is constant in x4 only if no charge flows through the boundary of the slice x4 = const, which at the degenerate points z = n Pi/2 is an ASSUMED no-flux condition)
